Two-Stage Single-Arm Design for Time-to-Event Endpoints

two_stage_single_arm_tte.Rd

Calculate optimal two-stage single-arm phase II trial design with a time-to-event endpoint using the one-sample log-rank test. This implementation is based on the methodology described in Wu et al. (2020).

Usage

two_stage_single_arm_tte(
  shape = NULL,
  S0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  hr,
  x,
  rate,
  alpha = 0.05,
  beta = 0.2,
  dist,
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

shape

Numeric. Shape parameter for the parametric survival distribution under the null hypothesis.

S0

Numeric. Survival probability at fixed time point x0 under the null hypothesis.

x0

Numeric. Fixed time point at which S0 is specified.

hr

Numeric. Hazard ratio under the alternative hypothesis (proportional hazards model). Values < 1 indicate improvement.

x

Numeric. Restricted follow-up time period for each patient.

rate

Numeric. Constant accrual rate (patients per time unit).

alpha

Numeric. Type I error rate (one-sided). Default is 0.05.

beta

Numeric. Type II error rate. Default is 0.2 (80% power).

dist

Character. Distribution under the null hypothesis. Options are:

  • "WB": Weibull distribution

  • "LN": Log-normal distribution

  • "GM": Gamma distribution

  • "LG": Log-logistic distribution

  • "SP": Logspline distribution (requires data argument)

data

Data frame. Required only when dist = "SP". Must contain columns time and status for fitting logspline distribution.

Value

A list with three elements:

param

Data frame of input parameters

Single_stage

Data frame with single-stage design parameters: nsingle, tasingle, csingle

Two_stage

Data frame with two-stage design parameters: n1, c1, n, c, t1, MTSL, ES, PS

Details

The function implements the optimal two-stage design algorithm described in Wu, Chen, Wei, Weiss, and Chauhan (2020). The design allows for early stopping for futility at the first stage based on a one-sample log-rank test.

The design parameters are:

  • n1: Sample size for stage 1

  • c1: Critical value for stage 1 (stop if Z1 ≤ c1)

  • n: Total sample size

  • c: Critical value for final analysis (reject H0 if Z > c)

Four parametric distributions are supported:

  • Weibull: S(t) = exp(-(t/b)^a)

  • Log-normal: S(t) = 1 - Φ((log(t) - μ)/σ)

  • Gamma: S(t) = 1 - I_a(t/b)

  • Log-logistic: S(t) = 1/(1 + (t/b)^a)

References

Wu, J., Chen, L., Wei, J., Weiss, H., & Chauhan, A. (2020). Optimal two-stage phase II survival trial design. Pharmaceutical Statistics, 19(3), 214-229. doi:10.1002/pst.1983

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example from Wu et al. (2020) - Small-cell lung cancer trial
# Weibull distribution with 5 months restricted follow-up
design <- two_stage_single_arm_tte(
  shape = 1.47327,
  S0 = 0.5,
  x0 = 3.5,
  hr = 0.5913,
  x = 5,
  rate = 2,
  alpha = 0.05,
  beta = 0.2,
  dist = "WB"
)

print(design)
} # }
